problems.title: 11. Remove duplicates from Sorted array
problems.description: Given a sorted array of integers, remove duplicate values in-place so that each distinct value appears exactly once at the beginning of the array. Return the number of distinct elements. The order of the distinct elements must remain the same. Input format: Line 1 contains n. Line 2 contains n sorted integers. Output format: Print the number of distinct elements, followed by a newline, then print the first k elements of the modified array on the next line, where k is the returned number of distinct elements. If n is 0, print 0 followed by a blank line. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000; the array is sorted in non-decreasing order.

visibleTestCases.explanation: There are three distinct values: 1, 2, and 3.
All values are already distinct, so the array remains unchanged.
All five values are equal, so only one distinct value remains.

problems.title: 12. Left Rotate Array by One
problems.description: Given an array of n integers, left rotate the array by exactly one position. The first element moves to the end, and every other element shifts one position to the left. Input format: Line 1 contains n. Line 2 contains n integers. Output format: Print the rotated array on one line, with elements separated by spaces. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: The first element 1 moves to the end, while all other elements shift left.
After one left rotation, 10 moves to the last position.
An array with one element remains unchanged after rotation.

problems.title: 13. Left Rotate Array by K Places
problems.description: Given an array of n integers and a non-negative integer k, left rotate the array by k positions. Each left rotation moves the first element to the end. Rotations beyond n positions wrap around, so rotating by k positions is equivalent to rotating by k mod n positions. Input format: Line 1 contains n. Line 2 contains n integers. Line 3 contains k. Output format: Print the rotated array on one line, with elements separated by spaces. Constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000; 0 <= k <= 1000000000.

visibleTestCases.explanation: Two left rotations move 1 and 2 to the end.
After three left rotations, the first three elements move to the end.
Rotating by the array length returns the array to its original order.
